tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursively solve remaining disks after placing largest
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After moving the current largest needed disk to its goal peg, solve the subproblem of moving the remaining smaller disks onto the same goal using recursion.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the largest disk for the current subgoal is correctly placed on its destination peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Continuing to move smaller disks before the largest disk is fixed, leading to unnecessary or illegal moves.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Standard recursive transfer of k disks
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To move a stack of k disks from a source peg to a target peg, first recursively move the top k‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, then move the kth disk, and finally move the k‑1 disks onto the target.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to relocate a contiguous stack of k disks between two pegs.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move the whole stack at once without first clearing the top k‑1 disks, causing an illegal placement.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final parseable block
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The answer must end with a single syntactically correct Python‑style list of moves; the parser extracts the last such list.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After all reasoning is done, before any trailing whitespace.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Providing moves on separate lines or missing brackets, so the parser cannot read a valid list.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Verify final configuration before output
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Mentally replay each move from the initial state to confirm that the final arrangement matches the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Just before writing the final move list.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Submitting a move sequence that leaves a disk on the wrong peg, causing the verifier to reject it.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Provide only the move list, no extra text
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The response should consist solely of the move list; any explanatory text can push the list beyond the token limit or be ignored.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Including a sentence like 'Here is the solution:' before the list, which may cause truncation.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate legality of each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before adding a move, ensure the source peg's top disk matches the moving disk and the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 3 onto a peg whose top disk is disk 2, violating the size rule.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear target peg of smaller disks before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Never place a larger disk onto a peg that currently holds any smaller disk; first relocate those smaller disks elsewhere.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Right before moving a larger disk onto its destination peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 4 onto a peg that still has disk 2 on top.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Avoid moving small disks onto a peg that will later receive a larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Do not place a small disk on a peg if a larger disk still needs to be moved onto that same peg later, unless you plan to move the small disk away first.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When deciding where to temporarily store a small disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Putting disk 1 on the final target peg, then later trying to move disk 2 onto that peg, which is illegal.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Move blocking smaller disks to any other peg (auxiliary or target) before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If a larger disk is not the topmost on its source peg, relocate the smaller disks above it to any other peg (including the auxiliary or the target) before moving the larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever a larger disk is blocked by smaller disks on its source.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move disk 5 while disk 3 sits on top of it on the same peg.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model stops generating before emitting any moves, often due to token limits or forgetting to output the answer.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always end the response with a non‑empty list of moves; verify that the list is present before submitting.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: Excessive reasoning or formatting before the list consumes the token budget, causing the list to be cut off.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Output only the move list, keep it short, and place it as the final content.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Attempted to move a disk that is not the topmost on its source peg
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model loses track of the current stack ordering while planning moves.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Before each move, check the current top of the source peg and only move that disk.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Prematurely moving a smaller disk onto the final target peg, causing later moves to be impossible
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model does not anticipate that a larger disk must later occupy that peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Reserve the final target peg for larger disks first; move small disks onto it only after all larger disks are placed.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Attempted to place a larger disk onto a smaller disk (illegal move)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model fails to enforce the size ordering rule when selecting destination pegs.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Check that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk before committing the move.
